subject: Follow-up: dedicated capacity & isolation needs for NovaPharm
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novapharm.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@novapharm.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: dedicated capacity & isolation needs for NovaPharm

Hi Samir / Lena —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Brief recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations. I captured what we discussed and a recommended path to move to a reserved (dedicated) GPU pool:  

Key pain points you described:
- Unpredictable inference latency at peak (p99 spikes > 1.2s impacting batch processing).
- Data isolation needs for PHI-adjacent models — you need tenant-level logical separation and audit trail for model inputs.
- Cost volatility when using spot/ephemeral instances during big experiments.

Goals we heard:
- Stable p50/p95 latency targets for production endpoints: p95 <= 300ms for short-form prompts (~128 tokens), p99 best-effort with fallbacks.
- Tenant isolation for the drugs team (separate pool or strict namespace-level isolation).
- Predictable monthly cost within a +/- 10% window.

Recommended initial configuration (Redwood suggestion):
1) Reserved pool: 4 x A100-80GB equivalent slots dedicated to NovaPharm (supports up to ~120 rps at 128-token profiles with batching).
2) Isolation: logical tenant isolation + optional dedicated node assignment for the drugs team; audit logs forwarded to your SIEM (we can onboard your Splunk instance).
3) Burst policy: additional 2-slot burst buffer for short windows (5–10 minutes) to absorb training/experimentation spikes — billed at a reduced burst rate.
4) SLA targets: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool; latency SLOs per model class (we'll propose concrete numbers after we run a 48-hour load simulation).

Open questions / asks from our side:
- Can you share rough qps/throughput distribution (dev vs prod) and a couple of representative prompt sizes?
- Are there any regulatory/compliance constraints beyond SOC 2/PCI (e.g., specific retention rules for PHI)?

Next steps (proposed):
- We will deliver a one-pager summary and an initial SLA draft (attached).
- Jordan (cc'ed) will follow up with a short ops checklist and a suggested runbook for failover/fallback.
- Schedule a 30-min technical walkthrough (Hannah + Jordan + your infra lead) to validate throughput assumptions: propose Wed 07/28 10:00 PDT.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-onepager.pdf (summary), sla-draft-novapharm.xlsx (initial SLA + pricing sketch)

Thanks — happy to adjust based on what matters most to you.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity & isolation needs for NovaPharm

Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. This looks very close to what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:  

1) Throughput: our current production is ~40 rps (128 tokens) with occasional daily spikes to ~160 rps during model refreshes and A/B experiments. Dev/staging sits at ~10 rps.
2) Isolation: the legal team wants a bind-mounted separation for the drugs model artifacts (we can provide the compliance contact). Logical tenant isolation is acceptable for the rest of the teams.
3) SLA: 99.9% availability sounds reasonable; for latency we need p95 <=350ms (not 300ms) across the drugs model and auto-fallback to a lower-cost variant if latency spikes.

Questions:  
- How will the burst billing be computed — flat hourly or per-minute?
- Can you run the 48-hour load sim using our anonymized prompts? We can provide a redacted data sample.

We're happy to do the technical walkthrough on Wed 07/28 10:00 PDT. Please send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Samir

Subject: Ops notes and proposed runbook for NovaPharm (short)

Hi all — quick ops input after reviewing the notes and sample qps you sent. High-level feasibility: confirmed. A few specifics and the short runbook below.

Feasibility notes:
- 4 reserved A100-equivalent slots will comfortably support base production (40 rps) with room for batching. To hit 160 rps spikes we recommend the 2-slot burst buffer + an autoscale window that adds 1 extra slot if sustained >120 rps for 3 minutes.
- Bind-mounted artifact isolation: we can implement a dedicated node pool for the drugs model with mount-level isolation and separate encryption keys. This will require an onboarding checklist item for your compliance team (IAM mapping + KMS access).
- Monitoring hooks: telemetry to include per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency, token-level billing, and KV-cache hit rates. We'll provide Grafana dashboards and a Prometheus scrape config.

Short runbook (15 items, compressed):
1) Pre-deploy smoke test (synthetic prompts)
2) KV cache warm with representative prompts
3) Confirm KMS access and mount permissions
4) Start traffic at 25% ramp for 5 minutes
5) Validate p95 latency and error rate thresholds
6) If sustained >120 rps for 3 minutes, enable 1 additional slot (autoscale)
7) If burst usage > 20% of allocated for 10 minutes, notify infra lead
8) Fallback model: route to quantized variant with warning header and increase cache TTLs
9) On fault, failover to alternate region with read-only mode for model artifacts
10) Post-mortem template + automated log bundle collection
11) Billing reconciliation step (daily usage export)
12) Audit log verification (forward to Splunk)
13) Quarterly SLA review cadence
14) On-call rotation and escalation path
15) Decommission plan for test pools

Next actions assigned:
- Jordan: produce full runbook doc + Grafana dashboard template (ETA 72 hours).
- Hannah/Stephanie: finalize commercial terms and deliver calendar invite for Wed 07/28 10:00 PDT (Hannah to send).
- Samir: share redacted prompt samples for the load simulation.

I'll attach the ops checklist to the Drive folder for NovaPharm.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Principal Cloud Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference
